Rashi on Shabbat 137b:11:1.hebrew: תולין את המשמרת - שמסננין בה שמרי יין, ומותח פיה לכל צד בעגול ונעשה כאהל על חלל הכלי שקורין אשטנד"א. ואע"ג דעביד אהל, שרי בי"ט כדמפרש בגמרא. אבל בשבת, מיתלא לכתחילה — לא; אבל אם תלויה היא, נותנין לתוכה שמרים ומסנן, דאין דרך בורר בכך:
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:11:1.english: One may suspend the strainer - With which one strains wine lees, and one stretches its opening to every side in a circle, and it becomes like a tent over the hollow of the vessel called estande [a vat]. And even though one is making a tent, it is permitted on a Festival, as is explained in the Gemara. However, on Shabbat, suspending [it] initially is not [permitted]; but if it is [already] suspended, one may put lees into it and strain [them], for this is not the normal manner of selecting.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:13:1.english: The window shutter - Such as [that of] a roof skylight.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:14:1.english: Except [with regard] to adding - Such as this [window] shutter, which is merely a temporary addition to the tent.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:15:1.hebrew: סבר ליה כרבי יהודה - הלכך הכא שרי, דמכשירי אוכל נפש הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:15:1.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - Therefore, here [on a Festival] it is permitted, for it is [an act] facilitating food preparation.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:16:1.hebrew: שאי אפשר לעשותן מעי"ט - כגון שפוד שנרצם בי"ט:
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:16:1.english: That cannot be performed on the eve of the Festival - For example, a spit that broke on the Festival.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:17:1.hebrew: עדיפא - חזקה, דהוא שרי אפילו מכשירין שאפשר מעיו"ט:
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:17:1.english: Exceeds - [It is] stronger, for he permits even preparatory [acts] that could [have been performed] on the eve of the Festival.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:19:1.english: [If] one hung a jug on a peg - He hung a small vessel on a peg.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:19:2.hebrew: ה"נ דמיחייב - והכא מאי חיובא איכא באהל עראי? בנין גמור לא הוי, ומדרבנן הוא דמיתסר:
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:19:2.english: Is he also liable - And here, what liability is there for a temporary tent? It is not a complete building, and it is [only] by rabbinic law that it is prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:2:1.hebrew: רוב גובהה - לא תימא רוב העטרה דקתני מתני' רוב היקפה, אלא אפילו רוב גובהה במקום אחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:2:1.english: Most of its height - Do not say [that] "most of the corona" that the Mishnah teaches [means] most of its circumference; rather, even most of its height in one place.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:3:1.hebrew: קטן המסורבל בבשר - פלטר"י בלע"ז, ששמן ועב, ולאחר שנימול נראה כמכסהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:3:1.english: A child who is encumbered with flesh - *Paltri* in Old French, [meaning] that he is fat and thick, and after he is circumcised, [the flesh] appears as though covering [the circumcision].

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:4:1.hebrew: כל זמן שמתקשה - ומתוך הקישוי מתפשט בשרו. בדשמואל גרסינן "ונראה מהול", במתניתא גרסינן "ואינו נראה מהול":
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:4:1.english: As long as when it hardens - And through the hardening, his flesh stretches out. In [the statement of] Shmuel, we read: "and it appears circumcised"; in the baraita, we read: "and it does not appear circumcised."

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:5:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו נראה ואינו נראה - לשמואל, נראה מהול הוא דאין צריך למולו, הא נראה ואינו נראה צריך. למתניתא, אינו נראה הוא דצריך, הא נראה ואינו נראה אינו צריך:
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:5:1.english: There is [a difference] between them [where] he appears and does not appear [circumcised] - According to Shmuel, it is [specifically] one who appears circumcised who does not need to be circumcised, but [one who] appears and does not appear [circumcised] does need [it]. According to the baraita, it is [specifically] one who does not appear [circumcised] who needs [it], but [one who] appears and does not appear [circumcised] does not need [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:7:1.english: Who made the beloved one holy from the womb - It calls Isaac "beloved," after [the verse] "whom you love" (Genesis 22).

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:7:2.hebrew: מבטן - דקודם שנולד נתקדש למצוה זו, דכתיב (שם יז) אבל שרה אשתך וגו' והקימותי את בריתי אתו, היינו מילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:7:2.english: From the womb - For before he was born, he was sanctified for this commandment, as it is written (Genesis 17): "But Sarah your wife, etc., and I will establish My covenant with him" — this is circumcision.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:7:3.english: In his flesh [bish'ero] - [Meaning] in his flesh [bivsaro].

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:7:5.english: And his offspring - [Those who come] after him.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:7:6.english: He sealed with the sign - this [sign] of the holy covenant.

Rashi on Shabbat 137b:7:7.hebrew: צוה להציל ידידות שארינו משחת - מגיהנם, דכתיב: "גם את בדם בריתך שלחתי אסיריך מבור אין מים בו" (זכריה ט׳:י״א):
Rashi on Shabbat 137b:7:7.english: Commanded to deliver the beloved of our flesh from destruction - From Gehenna, as it is written: "As for you also, by the blood of your covenant, I have sent forth your prisoners from the pit in which there is no water" (Zechariah 9:11).

Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:11:1.hebrew: תולין. אבל נותנין לתלויה ביום טוב - וצריך לפרש ולומר שאם היה עושהו מאתמול לא היה טוב כל כך וחזק. והא דתניא בפרקין דלעיל (שבת ד' קלד. ושם), דאין מסננין את החרדל במסננת שלו בי"ט — אם היה עושהו מאתמול לא היה מתקלקל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:11:1.english: One may suspend... However, one may place [wine] through a suspended [strainer] on a Festival. - And one must explain and say that if one had done it the previous day, it would not be as good and strong. And [regarding] that which was taught in a Baraita in our previous chapter (Shabbat 134a, and there [in the parallel passages]), that one may not strain mustard in its strainer on a Festival — [there,] if one had done it the previous day, it would not spoil.

Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:17:1.hebrew: דרבי אליעזר עדיפא מדר"י - תימה: ולר"א תיקשה ליה הנהו קראי דדריש בפ"ק דמגילה (ד' ז:), דקאמר: "ורבי יהודה, כתיב 'הוא' וכתיב 'לכם', ולא קשיא: כאן במכשירין שאפשר וכו'"? וכ"ת ר"א הוה דריש "הוא" לדרשה אחרינא — א"כ, מנ"ל התם דרבי יהודה הוה מפליג? לימא דרבי יהודה הוה דריש ליה לדרשה אחריתי כר' אליעזר. ונראה דבדאורייתא מודה ר' אליעזר דמכשירין דאפשר אסורים, וכי שרי להו הכא — ה"מ באהל עראי, דאינו אלא מדרבנן, גזירה אטו אהל קבע, כדאמרינן בביצה בפרק המביא (ד' לב:). מיהו קשה: מנ"ל דעדיפא? דילמא בהא מודה אפילו רבי יהודה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:17:1.english: [The leniency] of Rabbi Eliezer exceeds that of Rabbi Yehuda - This is perplexing: according to Rabbi Eliezer, should not those verses that [the Gemara] expounds in the first chapter of Megillah (7b) pose a difficulty for him, where it says: "And [as for] Rabbi Yehuda — it is written 'it [alone]' [and] it is written 'for you,' and [there is] no difficulty: here [it refers] to preparatory acts that can [be performed before the Festival], etc."? And if you say that Rabbi Eliezer expounded "it [alone]" for a different exposition — if so, from where do we know there [in Megillah] that Rabbi Yehuda made a distinction? Let us say that Rabbi Yehuda expounded it for a different exposition, like Rabbi Eliezer. And it appears that regarding biblical [prohibitions], Rabbi Eliezer concedes that preparatory acts that can [be performed before the Festival] are forbidden; and when he permits them here, that applies only to a temporary tent, which is only [prohibited] by rabbinic decree as a safeguard against [making] a permanent tent, as we say in Beitzah in the chapter [entitled] Hamevi (32b). However, it is difficult: from where do we know that [Rabbi Eliezer's leniency] exceeds [that of Rabbi Yehuda]? Perhaps regarding this even Rabbi Yehuda concedes:

Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:1:1.hebrew: מל ולא פרע את המילה כאילו לא מל - תימה, אמאי איצטריך למיתני האי? כיון דכבר תנא דבשר החופה את רוב העטרה מעכב המילה, וכי לא פרע — עדיין רוב עטרה מכוסה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:1:1.english: "If one circumcised but did not uncover [the membrane at] the circumcision, it is as if he had not circumcised" - [This is] astonishing: why was it necessary to teach this, since [the Mishnah] already taught that flesh covering the majority of the corona invalidates the circumcision, and when one has not uncovered [the membrane], the majority of the corona is still covered?

Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:6:1.hebrew: אבי הבן אומר כו' - רבינו שמואל גריס: "אבי הבן" ברישא, והדר "המל אומר"; וכבר הנהיג לעשות כן, לברך אבי הבן קודם המילה, משום ד"להכניסו" להבא משמע, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דפסחים (ד' ז. ושם): בלבער כ"ע לא פליגי דלהבא משמע, ועוד דכל המצות מברך עליהן עובר לעשייתן. ור"ת החזיר המנהג לקדמותו, וגרס "המל" ברישא והדר "אבי הבן", כמו שכתוב בכל הספרים. וכן מוכח כולה סוגיא, מדקאמר "העומדים שם אומרים כשם שהכניסו לברית" — מכלל שכבר הכניסו. ועוד, דגבי גר דבסמוך גרס ברישא "המל כו'" והדר "המברך אומר אקב"ו למול את הגרים", ונראה הוא שזהו כנגד ברכת אבי הבן; והתם א"א לשנות הגירסא, שיש באותה ברכה "להטיף מהן דם ברית כו' ברוך כורת הברית" — משמע דכל זה הוא אחר המילה, ועוד דהמברך מברך לעולם אחר המילה כמו במילת קטן. וההיא דפסחים ה"פ: בלבער כ"ע לא פליגי דלהבא משמע טפי מלשעבר, ומיהו לשעבר נמי משמע; כי פליגי ב"על ביעור" — מר סבר דמשמע מעיקרא טפי מלהבא, ומר סבר להבא נמי משמע כמו מעיקרא. והא דאמרינן דכל המצות מברך עובר לעשייתן — ה"מ כשהמברך עצמו עושה המצוה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:6:1.english: "The father of the child recites," etc. - Rabbeinu Shmuel reads "The father of the child [recites]" first, and afterward "The one who circumcises recites," and he already instituted the practice to do so — for the father of the child to recite the blessing before the circumcision — because "to bring him [into the covenant]" implies the future, as we say in the first chapter of Pesachim (7a and there): regarding "to remove" (le-va'er), everyone agrees that it implies the future; and furthermore, because for all commandments one recites the blessing prior to performing them. But Rabbeinu Tam restored the custom to its original state, and read "The one who circumcises" first and afterward "The father of the child," as is written in all the books. And so the entire sugya proves, from the fact that it says: "Those standing there recite: Just as he has brought him into the covenant" — [which implies] by inference that he has already brought him in. And furthermore, regarding a convert [in the passage] nearby, it reads first "The one who circumcises, etc.," and afterward "The one who recites the blessing says: Who has made us holy through His commandments and commanded us to circumcise converts," and it appears that this corresponds to the blessing of the father of the child. And there it is impossible to change the text, since in that blessing there is [the phrase] "to draw from them blood of the covenant, etc., Blessed [are You] who establishes the covenant" — [which] implies that all of this is after the circumcision, and furthermore because the one who recites the blessing always recites it after the circumcision, just as in the circumcision of a minor. And that [passage] in Pesachim is explained thus: regarding "to remove," everyone agrees that it implies the future more than the past, yet it also implies the past; where they disagree is regarding "concerning the removal" (al bi'ur) — one Master holds that it implies [what was done] beforehand more than the future, and one Master holds that it also implies the future just like [what was done] beforehand. And as for what we say, that for all commandments one recites the blessing prior to performing them — that applies [only] when the one reciting the blessing is himself performing the commandment.

Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:7:1.hebrew: ידיד מבטן - אומר ר"ת שהוא אברהם אבינו, שנקרא ידיד, שנאמר (ירמיהו י״א:ט״ו): "מה לידידי בביתי", כדדרשינן במנחות בפרק כל המנחות (מנחות ד' נג: ושם). ושלשת האבות נזכרים: "חוק בשארו שם" — הוא יצחק; "וצאצאיו חתם באות ברית קדש" — הוא יעקב. וצאצאיו — הוא ובניו, כמו שתרגם יונתן "הצאצאים והצפיעות" — "בניא ובני בניא" (ישעיהו כ״ב:כ״ד), כלומר: יוצאי צאצאיו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:7:1.english: The beloved one from the womb - Rabbeinu Tam says that this is Abraham our father, who is called "beloved," as it is stated (Jeremiah 11:15): "What has My beloved to do in My house?", as we expound in Menachot in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaMenachot (Menachot 53b and there[abouts]). And [all] three patriarchs are mentioned [in this blessing]: "marked the decree in his flesh" — this is Isaac; "and his descendants He sealed with the sign of the holy covenant" — this is Jacob. And "his descendants" [means] he and his sons, as [Targum] Jonathan translates "the offspring and the issue" [as] "the children and the children's children" (Isaiah 22:24), that is to say, those who issue from his offspring.

Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:9:1.hebrew: במצותיו וצונו למול את העבדים - שנאמר: "יליד בית ומקנת כסף" (בראשית י״ז:י״ב):
Tosafot on Shabbat 137b:9:1.english: "With His commandments, and commanded us to circumcise slaves" - As it is stated: "born in the house, or bought with money" (Genesis 17:12).
